source_scope: Only assigned source image, anonymous box TSV, generic blind rules, and generated crop manifest/crops were consulted. No witness, first TSV, first-pass page, report, draft, notes, hand log, comparison or adjudication was read.
general: The source boxes contain a list of conditions for a homomorphism and section, several revisions to the wording and local extension formulas, a displayed special-fiber membership expression, and an underlined transition with added extension/scindage phrases. The reading is visual only. No theorem, equivalence, identity or proof was checked or used to repair the text. Uncertainty remains on several compressed words, map-letter case, a nested round index, cancellation states and the crowded inserted condition in B015.

box_notes.note: Read as the single word équivalentes. An acute stands over the first small e, q has a long descender, and the final tall t is followed by e/s. The last tall stroke lacks a closed d bowl, favoring the ending -tes rather than a separate des. No terminal punctuation is visible.

The heading is a), then Cet hom est injectif. hom has no detached abbreviation stop. The long lower return at the right belongs to the final f, and the stroke entering from above at the left is the preceding q descender.

The large I has both upper and lower serifs, a low s and a separate prime; T has an upper bar. The relation is a wavy upper line over one straight lower line, read simeq. The beginning of cet is close to the crop edge but was visible in the whole source view. hom is followed by a colon, without an extra full stop.

Both k/K-like map letters have a tall stem and distinct branches; their case remains unresolved. The first complete formula is marked as a whole. Small circles separate the map letter, the parenthesized mu, and id. The id index is T. The phrase after the comma reads où, with a short grave-like upper stroke, then the repeated map letter est un. No extra stops are supplied.
The abbreviations hom and cont are left unexpanded and have no visible detached full stops. The horizontal map has a distinctly pointed right endpoint at pi. The final comma is separate.
et and mu are clear. N has a doubled left diagonal, represented by mathbb N. The raised final multi-stroke asterisk is retained; no punctuation is added.

The source writes lambda, a vertical restriction bar, and a baseline I. It is not silently changed into a subscript restriction. n'est pas l'hom trivial follows; the last word ends in a tall l-like return and no final stop. Lower clipped formula fragments belong to the insertion in B008.

The complete main word envisagée and the revision after it are included. The raised formula phrase begins E indexed by tilde f, then de E with a densely retraced U/K-like nested index and a tilde eta, then sur E indexed by tilde eta. A long curved leader runs from this phrase back to the gap after envisagée. No independently separable cancelled letter is asserted within the retraced index. The following short live word favors ne, but en is retained as an alternative from its compressed strokes. A long horizontal strike crosses the lower word question; provient is written above it, with a long p descender and final t-like return. Clipped upper ordinary text is excluded.

The first nested U-like index is retraced but not clearly separately cancelled. Both final round low glyphs have a wavy mark above and favor numeral 0; capital O remains an alternative. The complete mathematical terms are marked doubtful rather than normalized from their possible meaning. sur is legible between them.
The long strike crosses régulière. The accented e forms, g descender, l ascender and final è/r/e sequence remain recoverable. The clipped preceding word ending at the left is excluded.

The upper mark above f is wavy, with a rise, fall and terminal rise, so tilde is preferred. The mark above U is a single arch/caret, represented by a hat. de and sur are live; no terminal stop occurs in this box.

The complete isolated final symbol is a small s followed by a large closing parenthesis. Its lower turn is retraced. The preceding en is clipped at the left and is not duplicated in the box reading. No mark above s or following punctuation is added.

The label resembles f) with additional crossing/retracing; cancellation of the label is preferred but not secure. Si also has a crossing middle stroke whose status may be ordinary letter connection, so its deletion state is explicitly doubtful. Désignons par is raised above the baseline and attaches before the live tilde f. The later words désigne aussi are crossed by a continuous long line. The clipped upper context is excluded.

The live tilde f is followed by a crowded word tentatively read alors. Its first small bowl and tall loop, later round o-like trace and final r/s-shaped strokes support that reading. A line through the word may be a cancellation, but the connections are not sufficiently separate to decide; both deletion states are retained. The following hooked comma is live and separate.

The lower crossed passage begins with an exists-like symbol having three leftward bars and a curved right side. The following dark narrow glyph favors i but could be f under the crossing; tel que remains readable. The entire lower passage has a long cancellation. The raised replacement begins i followed by an open membership sign with a short middle bar, then I with a parenthesized k/K-like letter. The final relation has a visibly wavy upper stroke and one lower bar; it is retained as simeq despite the unresolved mathematical reading. The final two marks favor a semicolon with a hooked lower stroke, colon alternative. The full inserted formula is doubtful; no expected condition or missing sign is supplied.
The first large O has overlapping loops, followed by a low n. The separate final small black oval has an internal light center and is read as a, not as a dash or stop: On a.

The displayed formula reads tilde f(s) in I equals X_s setminus U_s, with a separate round final stop. The set difference sign is a short descending diagonal. Two tiny isolated dark points lie above the closing-parenthesis zone; they are noted as unattached marks rather than assigned a new superscript or punctuation role. A clipped stroke from adjacent text enters the upper edge. No mathematical identity is checked.

One continuous underline lies below the whole phrase. The short initial strokes favor on but do not yield a secure looped o, so this short word is marked doubtful. The following p/o/u sequence is clear, and the separated low final strokes favor pourra; pouvons is retained as an alternative. donc has a tall d and low remaining letters. The initial short strokes are not interpreted as an equals sign: they sit above the long underline and approximately beside one another.

Both the upper complete word décomposition and the lower revision are included. The underline belongs to the upper phrase. The upper formula has N indexed by s prime, simeq, and E with tilde K; the far-right K reaches the crop boundary and was visible in the whole source view. Below, the crossed symbol resembles pi with a low s/3-shaped index. The live replacement is E indexed by X_s, followed by a comma. The raised insertion reads ext. de E indexed by k(s)/K(s), par pi, with both the abbreviation stop and final comma visible. Its leader returns to the gap after the main E_X_s comma and before qui est. The inserted E is block-like with three bars; the index case remains uncertain. The two commas are separately retained.

The small raised un is accompanied by a V-shaped insertion caret attaching between dans and N(L_i). The caret is not a mathematical vee. N and L are capital; the small i is lower at the right of L. The separate point after the closing parenthesis is retained.

The long upper insertion reads E with nested U/eta, sur E_K, followed by a compressed ou/on. No separate tilde is securely visible over that first eta or K. Its under-brace-like leader points into the gap between the clipped ending of scindage and the existing de, so it is placed before de without supplying an additional de. The lower E has U indexed by tilde eta and is not visibly struck. A separate raised E_X_s is retained as an insertion between that term and sur, without silently deleting the first term. The final E has a sharp K with a wavy upper mark, followed by a comma. Clipped preceding-word and next-line fragments are excluded.
Lower-margin folio 89: two-loop 8 and a looped 9 with a long descending tail. No punctuation.
